plan_a_advantages: Includes a tempo run for speed endurance development.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a dedicated tempo run and a longer, controlled effort run, which are crucial for developing speed endurance – a key component of trail running speed. Plan B, while including interval training, relies heavily on cross-training and easier runs, which, while beneficial for recovery and consistency, don't directly target the specific adaptations needed to improve speed. Plan A’s structure prioritizes the development of the physiological attributes required for faster trail running, while Plan B focuses more on maintaining a base level of fitness.
